notes.title: 1.9 Blueprints and Automatic Clock Speed
notes.notes:
[h1]1.9 Blueprints and Automatic Clock Speed[/h1][p][/p][h2]Blueprints[/h2][p]When choosing to place a machine, there is a new option to choose a blueprint. Blueprints are similar to outposts, except they have a limit and a calculated value associated with them and the contents of the blueprint can be duplicated. The value calculated for the blueprint will be how many copies of that blueprint you will need, which you can optionally set a limit on. In order to calculate a blueprint, you will need at least one limit on a machine inside the blueprint, so that it can define what a single copy of a blueprint is, and you will also need to either have a limit on the blueprint or hook the blueprint up to something outside of the blueprint that does have a limit, so that it can define how many copies of that blueprint are needed.
[/p][p]You can right click on a blueprint or outpost for its menu where there is a new option to toggle being a blueprint on or off. So you can switch between an outpost or a blueprint without having to remake anything.[/p][p][/p][p]There is also an Auto Round feature for the blueprint. Since you cannot make a partial blueprint, the Auto Round feature will automatically round the blueprint up to the next whole number. When this rounding happens, the values inside the blueprint will be adjusted down to show how much each copy of the blueprint gets used. When in Auto Round mode, the background for the limit field is set to black.[/p][p][/p][p]The default state of Auto Round can be set in the Machine Defaults section in the Settings menu as well as mass applied there. You can also mass apply this as toggling this setting for one machine also toggles it for all selected machines.[/p][p][/p][h2]Automatic Clock Speed Calculations[/h2][p]In the right click menu of machines with clock speed, next to the existing clock speed field are now minus and plus buttons. The minus button lowers the clock speed so that the calculated value of the machine is the next whole number up. The plus button raises the clock speed so that the calculated value of the machine is the next whole number down. This will not allow clock speeds greater than 250%.[/p][p][/p][p]There is a new Auto Round feature found in the right click menu of machines with clock speed, similar to blueprints. This one however automatically adjusts the clock speed down in order to round a machine’s calculated value up to the next whole number. While in Auto Round mode, the clock speed and limit input field have their backgrounds set to black. This is because Auto Round mode needs to automatically adjust those fields. Editing those fields will automatically toggle off Auto Round mode. Manually toggling off Auto Round mode will restore those fields to what you had entered before toggling Auto Round mode on.[/p][p][/p][h2]Numbers[/h2][p]In the Settings menu is a new Numbers section. This allows you to control how numbers are displayed in various places throughout the app. It allows toggling between showing the exact fractional amount or showing a decimal amount. When showing the decimal amount, it allows customizing how many decimal places it shows and what rounding scheme to use. In most places the default decimal amount is rounded to 2 decimal places and the rounding scheme is to the nearest, that is, normal rounding. The clock speed hover text however defaults to rounding to 4 decimal places, because that is the accuracy allowed in game for clock speeds, as well as rounding up instead of nearest to ensure enough capacity.[/p][h2]
Other Changes[/h2][p]When adjusting the clock speed, machine MK, or node purity while in Parts Per Minute mode, an entered limit will change to reflect this change. Many people where confused in scenarios when a limit of 60 parts per minute was entered and they overclocked to 200% and it was still set to 60 parts per minute. Now it will automatically change that limit from 60 to 120. In addition, the parts per minute limit will always reflect the outputted parts per minute regardless of the clock speed, machine MK or node purity set.
[/p][p]Added the backspace keybind to delete a machine in addition to the delete key.[/p][p]
As well as various bug fixes.[/p]

notes.title: Manual Calculator
notes.notes:
Added the ability to have different calculation modes.

[b]None Calculator:[/b]
This does no calculations, but feel free to enter numbers on machines for your own notes.

[b]Manual Calculator:[/b]
A new calculator mode that does not take into account how splitter/merger or priority splitter/mergers prefer to split. Priority splitters and mergers are useless in this mode. For ambiguous splits/merges, you must define it with values entered into machines, thus requiring more info entered than in Full mode. Like Full mode, this ensures that all inputs and outputs for a given machine are in the correct ratios and the values on the conveyors add up to their connected inputs and outputs. However if you enter more values than needed, it can create conflicting definitions, in which case extras will be ignored. Which ones are ignored is arbitrary and may spontaneously change, so don’t use conflicting values. This may also produce negative numbers or numbers higher than entered if other machines require it. It is your responsibility to enter the numbers sanely. Since this mode does not take into account how splitters and mergers prefer to split/merge, the numbers produced may not always equal what happens in game, so it is your responsibility to ensure your splitters and mergers split in the correct fashion when building in game. This mode is probably the most similar to using a spread sheet to calculate or how most other tools would calculate. This mode is very fast and will probably be near instantaneous except for extraordinarily large builds, where it will still be a reasonable amount of time.

[b]Full Calculator:[/b]
This is the existing calculator. It tries to model what would happen in game and takes into account how splitters and mergers prefer to split/merge evenly and also takes into account how priority splitters and merger prefer to use the top priority. You can enter limits or leave blank for unlimited and the calculator will tell you what would happen in game. This will never give you negative values or values greater than a limit entered, and all number entered can be used to limit. This mode may help you spot places where the splitting/merging preferences might cause a deadlock. Figuring out how things split/merge is a surprisingly hard problem and this mode may slow down greatly for larger builds.



[h3]Additional Changes:[/h3]

The settings menu has gotten large and needed to be split into sub menus. The new calculator setting can be found under General. The calculator mode is stored with a save file. You can set it to switch calculator modes if an incoming save is different than the current mode, with the option to prompt or not.

There is a new settings under Style that allows the coloring of machines red when the calculated value is negative or greater than the entered value. This can only happen with the manual calculator. There is also a setting to color orange when a machine’s calculated value does not match the entered value. This can happen in the Manual or Full calculator. An outpost will be colored if it contains any colored machines inside it. 

Added the ability to hold SHIFT when dragging a selection to append in addition to the existing ability to hold CTRL to toggle the selection when dragging.

Several minor bug fixes.


[h3]FAQ:[/h3]

Does the new Manual calculator fix the bug where everything goes to zero?

No. Because this is not a bug, it is a feature. Things go to zero because that is what would happen if you built it in game. The modeler is telling you that what you built is going to get all jammed up and everything will stop. This is caused by having too much or not enough of a resource somewhere. You need to either find an outlet for the extra or input some where it is needed.

The manual calculator may hit this scenario less because it does not model how splitters and mergers prefer to work, but this is a drawback, not an improvement. For example, in game, if you set up a recycled rubber/plastic loop with a three-way split from the rubber output as well as a three way split from the plastic output with only one going back into the loop for each, not enough rubber and plastic will be sent back into the loop to sustain it and eventually it will stop outputting rubber all together. The Full calculator will show this by everything going to zero. The manual calculator can solve this if you enter enough values, but you will have to manually note that the splitter is sending half the materials back into the loop and thus need to take this into account when building in the game and not use a plain old three-way split.

notes.title: Improved Steam Cloud Integration
notes.notes:
Improved the steam cloud integration.

Previously it was possible to accidentally overwrite and lose data. Added three new settings that are all on by default.

Auto-Import from cloud: When starting the app this will auto import the steam cloud save. This can now be turned off.

Prompt on change: When auto-importing, if the steam cloud save is different than the local save, it will prompt before overwriting the local save. This can be turned off to always overwrite.

Auto-Export to cloud: When closing the app, saving, or autosaving, it will export the save to the cloud. This can now be turned off.



The cloud save can also be manually imported from the import menu. When importing the cloud save, either manually from the import menu or automatically on app startup, you can press CTRL+Z or undo button in the menu to undo the cloud save import and go back to the local save.

notes.title: Auto Saving & Space Elevator Phases
notes.notes:
Auto-Save Feature:
Previously the Modeler only saved on app exit (or CTRL+S). This could result in loss of data if the app was killed or power was lost. Now the app auto saves every 5 minutes. In addition it creates backups every time it saves. The auto save feature can be toggled off in the settings menu if desired. In addition the save interval and the max number of saved backups can be adjusted in the settings. When using the import button, it now asks if you want to do a regular import or import a backup save.

Steam Cloud Sync:
The writing of the save file is now more robust and the possibility of corruption while saving has been eliminated in cases where bad things happen during the writing of the file (like loss of power). Previously it was possible for Steam Cloud Sync to read/write while the modeler was reading/writing, possibly resulting in a corrupt file and total loss of saves. Now with more robust file writing to reduce the chance of corruption and backup files just in case the worst does happen, it is now safe to allow synchronizing of the save file via steam across multiple machines.

Space Elevator Phases:
Each of the Space Elevator goals can now be found as a recipe.

Various minor bug fixes

notes.title: 1.6.0 - The OCD Update
notes.notes:
Input/Output Reordering:
For machines with multiple inputs or outputs, just drag the input or output you want to move, to the location you want to move it to, to reorder that input or output. Simple as that. No longer will you have to have your connections crossed because the inputs or outputs are in the wrong order. When reordering the inputs or outputs of an outpost, the outside and inside orders will always match, otherwise it could get quite confusing as to what matches with what if you have multiple of the same part type. You can even reorder the order of Priority Splitters/Mergers/Splurgers, however since this can get quite confusing, a box is drawn around these inputs/outputs when they are reordered to let you know that the bottom one is now high priority and the top is low priority.

Connection Styles:
In addition to the curves, you can now change connections to be either direct straight lines, or to be only horizontal and vertical straight lines. Choose the Curves, Direct, or 2D option in the settings for Connection Style.

Movable Connections:
You can now adjust the path your connection takes instead of having just the default direct path. To do this, drag the label on the connection to a new location. This will now turn that label into a waypoint and anchor it at that spot and the new path will go through that spot. You can also double left click the initial floating label to turn it into an anchored waypoint. If you want another waypoint on the path, double left click an existing waypoint and a new one will be spawned. If you want to get rid of a waypoint, double right click it to delete it. If you have deleted all the waypoints and are left with just the floating label, you can now double right click that to delete the whole connection.

These waypoints will not move if you move either of the machines they are attached to, however if you have both machines selected and move them together, then the waypoints will be moved with the machines. Keep in mind this also applies when the connection goes from the output of a machine, to the input of that same machine. If the machine is not selected the waypoints will not move with it. If the machine is selected the waypoints will move with it.

In the case of something like Instant Scrap, you may want to connect an output to an input on the same machine. In this case it’s not actually possible to click the connection’s label in order to anchor it as it will always be behind the machine. If you right click the part’s connection point to bring up the menu for that connection point, you will find a new Add Waypoint option. This adds a waypoint to an existing connection. This will now allow you to move the machine (as long as that machine is not selected) to view the anchored waypoint, which then can be dragged to the location of choice. You will also find a help button there that describes the basics of waypoints. Keep in mind that the first time you add a waypoint it will be at the same location as the previous label, so it might not look like it did anything, but the difference is is that that waypoint is now anchored to a spot whereas the previous label moved with the machine.

Snap to Grid:
In the settings menu, you will find the ability to snap machines and waypoints to a grid. To turn it on, toggle the switch to on. It also allows you to specify a grid size in case you do not like the default. This will only apply to newly moved and placed machines/waypoints. If you want to snap existing machines/waypoints, use the apply button and choose which machines/waypoints you want to snap. This can allow different grids in different locations if that pleases you.

There are two grids, one for machines and one for waypoints. You can make them the same or different, such as if you want finer grain control over waypoints for example.

Connection Align:
Right click a part’s connection point to bring up it’s menu. If there are any connections to other machines, you will have the option to Align With Connection. This will move the machine such that the connection is aligned with the other connection point. If there are no waypoints the connection line will be a perfectly flat horizontal line.

Drag Sensitivity:
This is part of an older feature. When trying to click something that can also be dragged, if the mouse moved more than 1 pixel between button down and button up, it would register it as a drag instead of a click. This made it hard for some people to click. A while back I adjusted that value to be 25 pixels, so you would need to move the mouse at least 25 pixels before it registered as a drag instead of a click. Now you can customize that value in the settings menu.

notes.title: Storage Containers
notes.notes:
You can now build storage containers. You can set the icon to regular, industrial, fluid buffer, or industrial fluid buffer.

You can also set the fullness of the container.
A full container can allow unlimited output, but the input cannot be greater than the output.
An empty container can allow unlimited input, but the output cannot be greater than the input.
A partially full container can allow unlimited input or output.
Input = Output locks the two to always being equal.

This can also give improvements in calculations. When using partially full, the inputs and outputs are unlimited so they do not depend on each other. This allows them to be calculated completely independently if there are no other connections linking them. A full container means the inputs don't effect the outputs, so there could be improved calculations there. An empty container means the outputs don't effect the inputs, so there could also be improved calculations there.

Also added dimensional depots. You can set the upload rate for them, or just use them in parts per minute mode.

Dimensional depots can be toggled on in the Summary's Output section as can Storage Containers that are taking extra parts. Storage Containers that are giving extra parts can be toggled on in the Input section.

Defaults values for Storage Containers and Dimensional Depots can be changed in the settings menu, with an optional button to apply any new settings to various groups of already placed machines.

notes.title: Bug Fix for Window Off Screen
notes.notes: If the screen configuration changed since the last running of the app, the app remembers where it was on the screen and may try to display outside of the new screen bounds. Added a check at app startup to ensure it is visible on a screen.

notes.title: Miner Types, Node Purities, Parts per Minute, Defaults & More
notes.notes:
Added the ability to toggle any machine to use parts per minute vs the number of machines. Parts per minute are in italics and number of machines are bolded. This effects both the entered limit and the displayed value. New "Machine Defaults" section in the settings allows you to toggle the default for placing new building of certain types. There is also an apply button to apply that default to certain sections of already placed machines, such as everything, current outpost, or selected.

Added the ability to specify Miner types, Mk.1, Mk.2, and Mk.3. These choices are reflected when calculating values in the summary panel and for entered limits when not in parts per minute mode.

Added the ability to set node purities for machines put on nodes with varying purities. They effect the calculations similar to changing machines.

Added the ability to set the belt input type for the awesome sink as the belt speed defines how many awesome sinks you would need.

Default limits are now customizable. This can also be found in the "Machine Defaults" section in the settings. The limit value depends on if parts per minute mode is set or not, so a limit of 60 you might want to change to a limit of 1 if you toggle off parts per minute. Clear the value entirely to have no default value for that machine type.

Added the Resource Well Pressurizer. Does nothing except looks pretty and is used for calculations in the summary panel such as power.

Geothermal Generators now how changeable purities instead of different recipes per purity. Sadly this change is not backwards compatible with old saves and any Geothermal Generators you have down will disappear and need to be replaced.

Alien Power Augmenters, unlike all other buildings, do not assume it has the inputs when nothing is connected. If the calculated value is less than the max entered, unlike all other buildings, it assumes you have built what you entered because they still generate power even with no inputs.

And as always, various small bug fixes.

notes.title: Summary Panel & Power Calculations
notes.notes:
[b]Summary Panel:[/b]

New button in the bottom left of the main window brings up a summary panel.

This summary panel has several different sections which you can customize. It also has a selector at the top to change what you are summarizing, such as everything, the current outpost, or just what is selected. There is even a button in the bottom right of the summary panel to pop it out into a new window if you want.

Power: Shows a summary of the power created and used, including averages and max used and min produced, net power, and even power boosts from Alien Power Augmenters.

Overclock: See the number of Power Shards and Somersloops needed. This rounds the number of machines up when calculating.

Output: See how many parts you are outputting. You can customize this to show Unused outputs (outputs that are highlighted in green). Used outputs (outputs that go to another machine that is not in your current summary selection). And Sunk (what is going to Awesome Sinks).

Output Sink Points: The same as output, but it shows the total sink values for each part.

Inputs: See how many parts you are inputting. You can customize this to show Unmade inputs (inputs that are highlighted in red). Made inputs (inputs that come from another machine that is not in your current summary selection). And Mined (parts that come from machines that have no inputs).

Input Sink Points: The same as input, but it shows the total sink values for each part.

Machines: The number of each type of machine needed (rounded up for each one placed).

Cost To Build: The total cost to build all the machines listed in the Machines section.


[b]Improvements:[/b]

* Improved calculation times in some scenarios. Specifically, adding a splitter with overflow to something with no limit, like an awesome sink prevents parts from backing up further up the line in game. If all connections between two sections have an overflow like this, the algorithm can now detect that the second section cannot backup into the first and thus the first section can be calculated independently of the second section, greatly improving calculation times.

* Changed mouse sensitivity. Previously if the mouse moved more than 1 pixel between button pressed and released it would count as a drag. This made it difficult to click sometimes as it would often register as a drag instead. Changed to have a buffer of 25 pixels. This also means that in order to drag something less than 25 pixels, you need to drag out at least 25 pixels to trigger the drag, then drag back.

* Added CMD keybinds in addition to CTRL for Macs. Added CTRL+Insert and SHIFT+Insert to copy and paste. Can paste at a location with middle mouse button.

* Approximate Tier information can be found on recipe descriptions.

* Buttons now have rounded corners


[b]Bug Fixes:[/b]

* Added somersloop overclocking to smelters

* Numerous small bug fixes

notes.title: Fixed Graphical Glitches with Popups
notes.notes: Wrote custom popup handling code instead of using built in popups as a small subset of users were experiencing extreme graphical glitches that appeared to be related to popups. Hopefully this fixes those issues. Most users will probably not notice any change.

notes.title: Multi Selection & Machine Titles
notes.notes:
Satisfactory Modeler now has the ability to select/multi-select machines. Click a machine or right click drag a box around machines to select them. You can then move the selected machines as a group, delete them, cut or copy them, and paste copies of them. Move machines into or out of outposts by cutting and pasting. Standard keybinds for cut, copy, paste, select all, and delete.

Outposts and machines can now have titles added to them to help with organization. You can even embed part icons in the title by wrapping the full part name in double colons like this: "60::Modular Frame:: Factory"

notes.title: Panning and Zooming
notes.notes:
You can now pan around and zoom in and out. Use the scroll wheel to zoom and drag the background to pan. Enjoy infinite room to build, but don't forget to use outposts for organization.

You can also scale the UI from the settings menu.

A quick start guide with basic info on how to use the app can be found in the menu help section.
